cover_letter:
Dear itsme team,

I'm applying for the Content Creator role at itsme. I currently split my time between freelance SEO work and a junior digital marketer role at Episto, where I write and publish SEO content for client websites and keep their pages current in WordPress and Shopify. My work has always sat where content, search and the web meet, and this role puts all three in the same job.

The part of the description I keep coming back to is the interviewing. Getting someone to explain their work once, properly, and then writing it down better than they said it — that's the bit I find genuinely satisfying. At Knowledge Experts I supported SharePoint digital workplace projects for ŞOK Market (4,000+ stores, ERP/POS integration) and Aras Kargo (an application gallery for 12,000 staff). I was not the person writing keynote decks there. I was the person who had to understand what the technical team meant and put it into structure and words that clients and visitors could follow. That habit is what I'd bring to partner interviews and customer stories here.

On the practical side: on-page SEO, keyword and topic research, titles, headings, meta descriptions, internal linking, plus GEO/AEO work — structured data, entity markup, llms.txt — as search shifts toward AI answer engines. HubSpot Content Marketing certified, Canva for visuals, HTML/CSS/JavaScript underneath. I built and run baverok.com and mirook.com myself, so CMS publishing and maintenance aren't a handoff for me.

Two things I want to be straight about. My keynote deck experience is limited to Canva and my own material; I'd be learning PowerPoint properly rather than arriving as an expert. And my Dutch is at writing B1 and improving — English I write fluently. I'd rather tell you that now than in a review cycle.

I'd like to help itsme's B2B story land in the Netherlands and beyond. Thank you for reading.

Baver Ok
